weeks.title: Classes, Objects and the Static World
weeks.summary: Is week aap Java mein class aur object ka farq, constructors aur `this`, static vs instance members, access modifiers, aur references ke saath pass-by-value ka asli matlab seekhoge.
concepts: **Class vs object**: class ek blueprint hai (fields + methods), object uska runtime instance jo heap par `new` se banta hai. `Student s;` likhne se object nahi banta, sirf ek **reference** variable banta hai; `s = new Student()` ke baad hi woh kisi object ko point karta hai, warna field ke roop mein uski value `null` hoti hai.

**Default values**: fields ko automatic default milta hai (`int` → 0, `boolean` → false, `double` → 0.0, object reference → null). Local variables ko koi default nahi milta: initialise kiye bina padhoge to compile error ('variable might not have been initialized').

**Constructor**: class ke naam wala special block, koi return type nahi (`void` bhi nahi). Agar aapne ek bhi constructor nahi likha to compiler ek no-arg **default constructor** de deta hai; ek bhi likh diya to woh free wala nahi milta. `this.x = x` field ko parameter se alag karta hai, aur ek constructor doosre ko pehli line mein `this(...)` se call kar sakta hai.

**static vs instance**: `static` field poori class ki ek hi copy hoti hai (jaise banaye gaye objects ka counter), instance field har object ki apni. `static` method kisi object ke bina chalta hai, isliye uske andar `this` nahi hota aur instance fields/methods seedhe (bina object reference ke) use karna compile error hai. Static member ko `ClassName.member` se access karna clean style hai.

**Access modifiers**: `private` (sirf usi class mein), default/package-private (koi keyword nahi; same package), `protected` (same package + subclasses), `public` (sab jagah). **Encapsulation**: fields `private` rakho aur validation wale methods do, taaki object kabhi invalid state (jaise negative balance) mein na jaaye.

**References aur aliasing**: `b = a` object copy nahi karta, sirf reference copy karta hai; ab dono ek hi object dekhte hain aur ek se kiya badlav doosre se dikhega. `==` references compare karta hai (kya dono same object hain?), content nahi.

**Pass by value**: Java hamesha value pass karta hai. Object ke case mein value ek reference hai, isliye method object ke fields badal sakta hai, lekin parameter ko naya object assign karne se caller ka variable nahi badalta.

example.problem: Ek fictional bank app ke liye `Account` class banao jo har naye account ko 1001 se shuru hone wala unique number de aur negative opening balance reject kare. Teen accounts (500, 0, 1200) banne ke baad teesre account ka number aur total accounts kitne honge?
steps: `created` static hai: saare `Account` objects ek hi counter share karte hain; `number` aur `balance` har object ke apne hain.
Pehla `new Account(500)`: check pass, created 0 → 1, number = 1001.
Doosra (0): created 2, number 1002. Teesra (1200): created 3, number 1003.
`number` `final` hai: constructor mein ek baar set hua, baad mein badla nahi ja sakta. Fields `private` hain, isliye bahar se sirf getters se padhe ja sakte hain.
`getCreated()` static hai, isliye `Account.getCreated()` se bina object ke call hota hai.
Answer: output **1003 3**.

mistakes: Ek parameterised constructor likh kar `new Point()` call karna. Free default constructor tabhi milta hai jab class mein koi constructor na ho; zaroorat ho to no-arg constructor khud likho.
Constructor mein `balance = balance;` likhna jab parameter ka naam bhi `balance` ho. Ye parameter ko khud mein assign karta hai aur field default (0) hi rehta hai. `this.balance = balance;` likho.
`main` (static) se seedhe instance field ya method use karna. Pehle object banao (`new Main()`) aur uske through use karo, ya soch-samajh kar member ko static banao.
revision: Reference variable object nahi hai; `new` se object banta hai.
Fields ko default value milti hai, local variables ko nahi.
Koi constructor na likho tabhi free no-arg constructor milta hai.
static = class ki ek copy; static method mein `this` nahi hota.
private < default < protected < public (visibility badhti hai).
Java pass-by-value hai; object ke liye reference ki copy jaati hai.

weeks.title: Inheritance, super and the Object Class
weeks.summary: Is week aap `extends` se inheritance, `super` aur constructor chaining, overriding vs overloading ka farq, aur `Object` class ke `equals`, `hashCode`, `toString` ko sahi tarah override karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Inheritance (`extends`)**: subclass superclass ke accessible fields aur methods le leta hai aur naye jod sakta hai. Java mein class sirf **ek** class extend kar sakti hai, aur har class aakhir mein `java.lang.Object` se aati hai. Rishta 'is-a' hona chahiye: `Manager extends Employee` theek hai, `Car extends Engine` nahi (wahan composition, yaani 'has-a', sahi design hai).

**Constructor chaining**: subclass ke har constructor ki pehli line ya to `this(...)` hoti hai ya `super(...)`; kuch na likho to compiler `super()` daal deta hai. Isliye object banate waqt constructors upar se neeche chalte hain: `Object` → parent → child. Agar parent mein no-arg constructor nahi hai to child ko explicitly `super(args)` likhna padega, warna compile error.

**Overriding**: subclass same signature (naam + parameter types) wala instance method dobara likhta hai. Rules: return type same ya covariant (subtype), access kam nahi kar sakte (`public` ko default ya `protected` nahi bana sakte), aur naye ya broader checked exceptions nahi phenk sakte. `@Override` lagao: signature galat hua to compiler pakad lega.

**Overloading**: same naam, alag parameter list. Kaunsa overload chalega ye **compile time** par arguments ke static (declared) types se tay hota hai. Sirf return type badalna overloading nahi hai, compile error hai.

**`super`**: `super.method()` parent ka version call karta hai aur `super.field` parent ka field. Dhyaan do: parent ke method ke andar se kisi overridden method ko call kiya to wahan bhi dynamic dispatch hota hai, yaani object agar child ka hai to child ka version chalega.

**`equals` aur `hashCode`**: `Object.equals` default mein `==` hai (same object?). Value-based equality chahiye to `public boolean equals(Object o)` override karo (parameter `Object` hi hona chahiye) aur saath mein `hashCode` bhi, taaki equal objects ka hash same ho; warna `HashMap`/`HashSet` mein objects 'kho' jaate hain.

**`toString`**: string concatenation aur `println` object par `toString()` call karte hain. Default output class ka naam aur ek hash jaisa hota hai, jo logs mein bekaar hai; isliye readable `toString` override karna professional practice hai.

example.problem: Fictional payroll system: `Employee(name, base)` aur `Manager extends Employee` jisme bonus bhi hai. `new Manager("Riya", 50000, 10000)` banane par kya print hoga, aur us object ka `pay()` aur `toString()` kya denge?
steps: `Manager` constructor ki pehli line `super(name, base)` hai, to pehle `Employee` constructor chalta hai aur "Employee ready" print hota hai.
Phir `bonus = 10000` set hota hai aur "Manager ready" print hota hai.
`pay()` Manager mein override hai: `super.pay()` (50000) + bonus (10000) = 60000.
`toString()` Employee mein likha hai, par uske andar `pay()` dynamic dispatch se Manager wala chalta hai.
`Employee` mein no-arg constructor nahi hai, isliye `super(name, base)` likhna zaroori tha.
Answer: do lines "Employee ready", "Manager ready"; `pay()` = **60000**; `toString()` = **Riya (60000)**.

mistakes: Parent mein sirf parameterised constructor ho aur child constructor `super(...)` na likhe. Compiler `super()` daalta hai jo exist nahi karta: compile error. Pehli line mein sahi `super(args)` likho.

`public boolean equals(Employee e)` likhna. Ye override nahi, overload hai; collections `equals(Object)` call karte hain aur aapka method kabhi nahi chalega. Parameter `Object` rakho aur `@Override` lagao.
Override karte waqt access kam kar dena, jaise `toString()` bina `public` ke likhna. Compile error 'attempting to assign weaker access privileges'.
revision: Constructors upar se neeche chalte hain: Object → parent → child.
Pehli line `this(...)` ya `super(...)`; kuch nahi to implicit `super()`.
Overriding = same signature, runtime par decide; overloading = alag parameters, compile time par decide.
Override mein access kam nahi; return type same ya covariant.
`equals(Object)` override karo to `hashCode()` bhi.

weeks.title: Polymorphism, Dynamic Dispatch and Casting
weeks.summary: Is week aap dekhoge ki superclass reference se method call karne par runtime object ka method kaise chalta hai, upcasting/downcasting, `instanceof` aur pattern matching, aur kyun fields aur static methods polymorphic nahi hote.
concepts: **Static type vs runtime type**: `Shape s = new Circle();` mein `s` ka static (declared) type `Shape` hai aur runtime type `Circle`. Compiler sirf static type dekhta hai: `s` par wahi methods call ho sakte hain jo `Shape` mein declared hain, chahe object kuch bhi ho.

**Dynamic dispatch**: overridden instance method ka kaunsa version chalega, ye runtime object tay karta hai. Isi se ek `Shape[]` par loop karke har shape ka sahi `area()` chal jaata hai, bina `if-else` ke. Naya shape jodna ho to sirf nayi class likho, purana loop wahi rahega (open–closed principle).

**Overload compile time, override runtime**: pehle compiler arguments ke static types se method signature chunta hai (overload resolution), phir runtime par us signature ka sabse specific override chalta hai. Ye do alag steps hain; tricky exam questions aksar isi se bante hain.

**Upcasting aur downcasting**: subclass se superclass reference (upcast) hamesha safe aur implicit hai. Ulta (downcast) ke liye explicit `(Dog) a` likhna padta hai; compile tabhi hota hai jab types ek hi hierarchy mein hon, aur runtime par object sach mein us type ka na ho to `ClassCastException`.

**`instanceof` aur pattern matching**: downcast se pehle check karo: `if (a instanceof Dog)`. Java 16+ mein `if (a instanceof Dog d) d.bark();` check aur cast ek saath kar deta hai. `null instanceof X` hamesha false hota hai.

**Fields aur static methods polymorphic nahi**: field access static type se resolve hota hai, isliye subclass mein same naam ka field parent wale ko sirf **hide** karta hai, override nahi. Static methods bhi hide hote hain; call reference ke static type se tay hota hai. Isliye fields `private` rakho aur overridable getters se padho.

example.problem: Fictional delivery app: `Vehicle` ke subclasses `Bike` aur `Truck` ke `costPerKm()` alag hain. Fleet ke har vehicle ke liye 10 km ka cost nikaalo, aur sirf `Truck` ke liye extra `loadCharge()` jodo.
steps: `fleet` ka element type `Vehicle` hai, par har element ka runtime type alag hai.
`Bike`: dynamic dispatch se `costPerKm()` = 6, cost = 60.
`Truck`: 25 × 10 = 250; `v instanceof Truck t` true hai, to `t.loadCharge()` (200) bhi judta hai: 450.
`v.loadCharge()` seedhe nahi likh sakte: `Vehicle` mein ye method nahi hai, compile error. Isliye pehle pattern-matching se cast kiya.
Plain `Vehicle`: 10 × 10 = 100.

mistakes: Bina check ke downcast karna (`(Truck) v`). Compile ho jaata hai par galat object par `ClassCastException`. Pehle `instanceof` (ya pattern matching) use karo.
Sochna ki subclass ka same-naam field parent reference se bhi dikhega. Fields static type se resolve hote hain; polymorphic behaviour ke liye methods use karo.
Overloaded method chunte waqt runtime type dekhna. Compiler argument ka declared type dekh kar signature chunta hai; sirf override runtime par decide hota hai.
revision: Compiler static type dekhta hai, JVM runtime type.
Override → dynamic dispatch; overload, fields, static methods → compile time.
Upcast implicit aur safe; downcast explicit, galat ho to `ClassCastException`.
`x instanceof T t` check aur cast ek saath karta hai.
`null instanceof T` hamesha false.

weeks.title: Abstract Classes and Interfaces
weeks.summary: Is week aap abstract classes aur interfaces se contracts design karna, default aur static interface methods, ek class mein kai interfaces implement karna, aur dono mein se kab kya chunna hai, ye seekhoge.
concepts: **Abstract class**: `abstract` class ka object `new` se nahi ban sakta. Isme abstract methods (sirf signature, body nahi) ke saath normal methods, fields aur constructors sab ho sakte hain. Abstract class ka constructor tab chalta hai jab uske kisi concrete subclass ka object banta hai.

**Abstract method ka rule**: jo class kisi inherited abstract method ko implement nahi karti, use khud `abstract` declare karna padta hai, warna compile error. Concrete (non-abstract) class mein ek bhi unimplemented abstract method nahi reh sakta.

**Interface**: ek contract ki 'ye type kya kar sakta hai'. Interface ke abstract methods implicitly `public abstract` hote hain aur fields implicitly `public static final` (constants). Isliye implement karne wala method `public` hi hona chahiye, warna weaker access ka compile error.

**Multiple interfaces**: class sirf ek class extend kar sakti hai par kai interfaces implement kar sakti hai: `class Drone extends Device implements Flyable, Recordable`. Isse ek type ke kai 'roles' ban jaate hain, bina state ki multiple inheritance ki problems ke.

**Default, static aur private methods** (Java 8/9+): `default` method body ke saath aata hai, taaki interface mein naya method jodne par purani implementing classes na tootein. Do interfaces same default method dein to class ko use override karna hi padega, aur `A.super.m()` se kisi ek ka version call kar sakte ho. Rule: class (ya superclass) ka method hamesha interface default se jeet-ta hai. Interface ke `static` methods `Name.m()` se hi call hote hain.

**Template method pattern**: abstract class algorithm ka skeleton ek `final` method mein rakhti hai aur badalne wale steps abstract chhodti hai. Data pipelines aur frameworks yahi karte hain: order fixed, steps pluggable.

**Kab kya**: shared state/code wali 'is-a' family ho to abstract class; alag-alag unrelated classes ko ek capability deni ho (`Comparable`, `Runnable`, `AutoCloseable`) to interface. 'Program to an interface': variable ka type interface rakho (`List<String> xs = new ArrayList<>()`), taaki implementation badalna aasaan rahe.

example.problem: Fictional analytics tool: har data source ko `DataSource` interface follow karna hai, aur abstract `Pipeline` class har source ke liye load → clean ka fixed order chalati hai. Program ka output kya hoga?

Doosri line: `clean(120)` dynamic dispatch se DropNulls ka chalta hai → 120 − 15 = 105.
Answer: "load: source with 120 rows" aur "clean: **105**".

mistakes: Interface method implement karte waqt `public` bhool jaana. Interface method implicitly public hai, to class mein default access weaker hai: compile error.
Abstract class ka object banana (`new Pipeline()`). Sirf concrete subclass ka object banta hai; abstract class reference type ke roop mein use hoti hai.
Do interfaces se same default method aaye aur class override na kare. Compiler conflict ka error deta hai; override karke `A.super.m()` ya apna logic likho.
revision: Abstract class: constructor, state, abstract + concrete methods; `new` nahi.
Interface methods implicitly `public abstract`, fields `public static final`.
Ek class extend, kai interfaces implement.
Class ka method > interface default; do defaults takraayein to override zaroori.
Variable ka type interface rakho, object concrete class ka.

weeks.title: Collections, Iterators and Ordering
weeks.summary: Is week aap Java Collections Framework ke `List`, `Set`, `Map` interfaces, ArrayList vs LinkedList ka cost, Iterator se safe removal aur `ConcurrentModificationException`, aur `Comparable`/`Comparator` se sorting seekhoge.
concepts: **Interface-first design**: `Collection` ke neeche `List` (order + duplicates allowed, index se access), `Set` (duplicates nahi) aur `Queue`/`Deque` hain; `Map` alag hierarchy hai (key → value, keys unique). Variable ka type interface rakho: `List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();` taaki implementation baad mein badal sako.

**ArrayList vs LinkedList**: ArrayList andar ek resizable array hai: `get(i)` O(1), end par `add` amortised O(1), beech mein insert/remove O(n) (elements shift hote hain). LinkedList doubly-linked nodes hai: `get(i)` O(n), par iterator ki current position par insert/remove O(1). Practice mein zyaadatar ArrayList hi tez padta hai (memory mein contiguous, cache-friendly).

**Set aur Map implementations**: `HashSet`/`HashMap` average O(1) dete hain par koi order guarantee nahi. `LinkedHashSet`/`LinkedHashMap` insertion order rakhte hain. `TreeSet`/`TreeMap` sorted order (O(log n)) rakhte hain aur uniqueness `compareTo`/`Comparator` se decide karte hain, `equals` se nahi.

**Iterator**: `hasNext()`, `next()`, `remove()`. for-each loop andar se iterator hi use karta hai. Iterate karte waqt collection ko seedhe (`list.remove(x)`) badloge to ArrayList ka fail-fast iterator agle `next()` par `ConcurrentModificationException` phenkta hai. **`remove(int)` vs `remove(Object)`**: `List<Integer>` mein `list.remove(2)` index 2 hata deta hai, value 2 nahi. Value hatani ho to `list.remove(Integer.valueOf(2))` likho.

**Comparable vs Comparator**: `Comparable<T>` class ka 'natural order' hai (`compareTo`, jaise String ka lexicographic). `Comparator<T>` bahar se alag orderings deta hai: `Comparator.comparingInt(...)`, `.reversed()`, `.thenComparing(...)`. Contract: negative = pehla chhota, 0 = barabar, positive = pehla bada.
**Overflow-safe compare**: `a - b` se compare karna bade ya negative numbers par int overflow kar sakta hai aur galat sign de sakta hai; `Integer.compare(a, b)` use karo.

weeks.title: Generics, Wildcards and Callbacks
weeks.summary: Is week aap generic classes aur methods likhna, bounded types, wildcards (`? extends`, `? super`), type erasure ki basic limits, aur interfaces aur lambdas se callbacks pass karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Generics kyun**: bina type ke `List` har cheez `Object` ki tarah rakhta tha, aur galat type ka pata runtime par `ClassCastException` se chalta. `List<String>` mein compiler hi galat `add` rok deta hai aur `get` par cast ki zaroorat nahi padti. Errors runtime se compile time par shift ho jaate hain.

**Generic class aur method**: `class Box<T> { T value; }` mein `T` type parameter hai. Generic method apna type parameter return type se pehle declare karta hai: `static <T> T first(List<T> xs)`. Call karte waqt compiler arguments (ya target type) se `T` infer kar leta hai.

**Bounded types**: `<T extends Comparable<T>>` ka matlab `T` aisa type hona chahiye jo khud se compare ho sake; tabhi method ke andar `x.compareTo(y)` likh sakte ho. Bound mein `extends` class aur interface dono ke liye likha jaata hai.

**Invariance**: `Integer` `Number` ka subtype hai, par `List<Integer>` `List<Number>` ka subtype **nahi**. Warna koi `List<Number>` reference se `Double` daal deta aur Integer list kharab ho jaati. Arrays covariant hain (`Object[] a = new String[2];` compile hota hai) aur galat store par runtime `ArrayStoreException` dete hain.

**Wildcards aur PECS**: `List<? extends Number>` se padh sakte ho (har element `Number` hai) par `null` ke alawa kuch add nahi kar sakte: ye producer hai. `List<? super Integer>` mein `Integer` add kar sakte ho, par padhne par sirf `Object` milta hai: ye consumer hai. Yaad rakho: Producer Extends, Consumer Super.

**Type erasure**: compile ke baad generic type arguments mita diye jaate hain; runtime par `List<String>` aur `List<Integer>` dono bas `ArrayList` hain. Isliye `new T()`, `new T[10]`, `x instanceof List<String>` allowed nahi, aur ek class mein `print(List<String>)` aur `print(List<Integer>)` dono nahi ho sakte (same erasure).

**Callbacks**: kisi method ko 'baad mein kya karna hai' woh code argument mein do. Java mein ye functional interface (sirf ek abstract method) se hota hai: `Comparator`, `Runnable`, `Function<T,R>`, `Predicate<T>`, `Supplier<T>`, ya apna interface. Lambda `(a, b) -> a + b` ya method reference `Integer::sum` us interface ka object ban jaata hai. Lambda bahar ke local variables tabhi use kar sakta hai jab woh **effectively final** hon.

example.problem: Ek generic `retry` helper likho jo koi bhi operation (callback) chalaye, fail hone par dobara try kare, aur jiska result type kuch bhi ho sake. Ek fictional flaky service pehli do calls mein fail hoti hai.

Callback ka type `Supplier<T>` hai: koi argument nahi, ek value return. Lambda isi interface ka object ban jaata hai.
Attempt 1: calls = 1 < 3, exception → "attempt 1 failed". Attempt 2: calls = 2, phir fail → "attempt 2 failed".
Attempt 3: calls = 3, lambda "OK after 3" return karta hai aur `retry` turant wahi value return kar deta hai.
Lambda `calls` ko badal paaya kyunki woh static field hai; agar `main` ka local variable hota to effectively-final rule ki wajah se compile error aata.
Answer: "attempt 1 failed", "attempt 2 failed", phir **OK after 3**.

mistakes: `List<Number> xs = new ArrayList<Integer>();` likhna. Generics invariant hain, ye compile error hai. Sirf padhna ho to `List<? extends Number>` lo.
`List<? extends T>` mein `add` karne ki koshish. Compiler ko exact element type nahi pata, isliye `null` ke alawa kuch add nahi hota. Likhna ho to `List<? super T>` lo.
Lambda ke andar local counter badhana (`count++`). Captured local effectively final hona chahiye; `AtomicInteger` ya field use karo, ya behtar, result ko loop/stream se return karo.
revision: Generics = compile-time type safety, cast ki zaroorat nahi.
`<T extends X>` bound `T` par X ke methods use karne deta hai.
`List<Integer>` `List<Number>` nahi hai; arrays covariant hain.
PECS: padhne ke liye `? extends`, likhne ke liye `? super`.
Erasure: runtime par type argument nahi bachta; `new T()` nahi likh sakte.
Lambda = functional interface ka object; captured locals effectively final.

weeks.summary: Is week aap reference copy, shallow copy aur deep copy ka farq, `Cloneable` aur `clone()` ke rules, byte vs character streams, aur `Serializable`/`transient` se objects ko bytes mein save karke wapas laana seekhoge.
concepts: **Teen tarah ki copy**: `b = a` sirf reference copy hai (ek hi object). **Shallow copy** naya object banata hai par andar ke reference fields (arrays, lists) wahi share karta hai. **Deep copy** andar ke mutable objects ki bhi nayi copies banata hai, taaki ek copy badalne se doosri na badle.

**`clone()` aur `Cloneable`**: `Object.clone()` protected hai aur field-by-field shallow copy deta hai. Class `Cloneable` (marker interface, koi method nahi) implement na kare to `super.clone()` runtime par `CloneNotSupportedException` phenkta hai. Common pattern: `public Team clone()` (covariant return type) override karo, `super.clone()` lo, phir mutable fields khud copy karo (`copy.scores = scores.clone()`).

**Alternatives**: copy constructor (`Team(Team other)`) ya static factory zyada clear aur type-safe hote hain, isliye kai teams `clone()` se bachti hain. Immutable fields (String, Integer) share karna safe hai; sirf mutable fields ko copy karna padta hai.

**Byte vs character streams**: `InputStream`/`OutputStream` raw bytes ke liye (images, binary files, network). `Reader`/`Writer` characters ke liye, jo charset (jaise UTF-8) se bytes ↔ chars convert karte hain. `InputStreamReader` byte stream ko character stream mein badalne wala bridge hai.

**Decorator layering**: streams ek doosre ko wrap karte hain: `new BufferedReader(new FileReader(f))` buffering aur `readLine()` jodta hai; `DataOutputStream` primitives likhta hai; `ObjectOutputStream` poore objects. Sabse bahar wala stream close karne se andar wale bhi close ho jaate hain.

**Serialization**: `Serializable` (marker interface) wali class ka object `ObjectOutputStream.writeObject` se byte stream ban jaata hai aur `readObject` se wapas aata hai. Har non-transient field ka type bhi serializable hona chahiye, warna `NotSerializableException`. Deserialization par us class ka constructor aur field initialisers nahi chalte; values stream se bhari jaati hain.

**`transient` aur `serialVersionUID`**: `transient` field (password, cache, connection) save nahi hota; wapas aane par uski default value (null/0/false) hoti hai. `private static final long serialVersionUID` class ka version batata hai; class badalne par mismatch se `InvalidClassException` aata hai, isliye ise explicitly declare karna achhi practice hai.

weeks.title: Packages, Access Across Packages and File I/O
weeks.summary: Is week aap packages aur imports se code organise karna, alag packages ke beech `public`, `protected` aur default access ke exact rules, try-with-resources, aur files padhna-likhna seekhoge.
concepts: **Package**: related classes ka namespace, jo file ki pehli statement hoti hai: `package com.shop.model;`. Folder structure package naam se match karti hai (`com/shop/model/Item.java`). Fully qualified naam (`com.shop.model.Item`) se alag packages ki same naam wali classes, jaise `java.util.Date` aur `java.sql.Date`, mein confusion nahi hota.

**import**: sirf naam chhota likhne ki suvidha hai, code copy nahi karta. `import java.util.List;` ek type laata hai, `import java.util.*;` us package ki saari types, par **subpackages nahi** (`java.util.function.Function` ke liye alag import). `java.lang` (String, Math, System) automatically imported hai. `import static java.lang.Math.max;` static members ke liye hai.

**Access across packages**: `public` sab jagah dikhta hai. Default (koi modifier nahi) sirf usi package mein; doosre package se use karna compile error hai. Packages hierarchical nahi hote: `com.shop` aur `com.shop.model` access ke liye bilkul alag packages hain. Top-level class sirf `public` ya default ho sakti hai, aur ek file mein ek hi public class jiska naam file ke naam jaisa ho.

**`protected` ka exact rule**: same package mein sab ke liye khula hai. Doosre package mein sirf subclass ke code ke andar, aur wahan bhi sirf subclass type ke reference ke through: `v` (yaani `this.v`) ya `Sub` reference se `s.v` theek hai, par `Base` type ke kisi aur reference par `other.v` compile error hai.

**try-with-resources**: `try (BufferedReader br = ...)` mein declared har `AutoCloseable` resource block khatam hote hi (normal ya exception, dono mein) automatically close hota hai, declaration ke **ulte** order mein, aur ye `catch`/`finally` chalne se pehle hota hai. Close ke dauran aayi exception main exception ke andar 'suppressed' ban kar judti hai.

**Files padhna/likhna**: `BufferedReader.readLine()` har call par ek line deta hai aur end par `null`. `new FileWriter(path)` file ko khaali karke likhta hai (overwrite), `new FileWriter(path, true)` end mein jodta hai (append). `PrintWriter` se `println` milta hai. NIO helpers: `Files.readAllLines(Path.of("a.txt"))`, `Files.writeString(...)`, `Files.lines(path)` (ye stream bhi close karni padti hai).

**Checked I/O exceptions**: `FileReader` ka constructor `FileNotFoundException` aur `readLine` `IOException` phenk sakte hain. Ye checked hain, to ya `try/catch` karo ya method par `throws IOException` likho, warna compile error.

`main` par `throws IOException` hai, isliye checked exceptions ko alag se pakadna zaroori nahi.
Answer: "**2 errors copied**", aur `errors.txt` mein 2 lines.

mistakes: `import java.util.*;` ko subpackages ke liye bhi kaafi samajhna. `java.util.function` ya `java.util.concurrent` ki types alag se import karo.
Doosre package se default-access field ya method use karna. Woh sirf apne package mein dikhta hai; zaroorat ho to `public` method do.
Reader/stream close karna bhool jaana, ya exception wale raste par close na hona. Hamesha try-with-resources use karo.
revision: `package` pehli statement; folder path = package naam.
`import pkg.*` subpackages import nahi karta; `java.lang` free hai.
Default access = sirf same package.
Doosre package mein `protected` sirf subclass ke andar, subclass type ke reference se.

weeks.title: Exception Handling in Depth
weeks.summary: Is week aap exception hierarchy (checked vs unchecked), try/catch/finally ka exact flow, `throw` vs `throws`, apni custom exceptions, multi-catch, aur `finally` ke saath `return` ke tricky cases seekhoge.
concepts: **Hierarchy**: `Throwable` ke do bachche hain: `Error` (JVM-level problems jaise `OutOfMemoryError`, `StackOverflowError`; inhe normally pakadte nahi) aur `Exception`. `RuntimeException` aur uske subclasses (`NullPointerException`, `ArithmeticException`, `IllegalArgumentException`, `IndexOutOfBoundsException`) **unchecked** hain; baaki exceptions (`IOException`, `SQLException`, `InterruptedException`) **checked** hain.

**Checked ka rule**: jo code checked exception phenk sakta hai, use ya to `try/catch` mein handle karo ya method signature mein `throws` declare karo; compiler isko enforce karta hai. Unchecked ke liye ye zaroori nahi; woh aksar programming bugs ya broken preconditions dikhate hain.

**Flow**: try mein exception aate hi try ka baaki hissa skip hota hai, upar se neeche pehla matching `catch` chalta hai (sirf ek), phir `finally`. Koi catch match na kare to `finally` chal kar exception caller ko propagate hoti hai. `finally` lagbhag hamesha chalta hai (exception, `return`, `break` sab ke baad); `System.exit` jaise rare cases chhod kar.

**catch ka order**: specific pehle, general baad mein. `catch (Exception e)` ke baad `catch (IOException e)` likhna compile error hai (wo catch kabhi pahuncha hi nahi ja sakta). Multi-catch `catch (IOException | SQLException e)` tab use karo jab handling same ho; dono types ek doosre ke subclass nahi hone chahiye.
**`throw` vs `throws`**: `throw new X(...)` ek exception object abhi phenkta hai (statement). `throws X` method signature mein batata hai ki ye method X phenk sakta hai (declaration).

**Custom exceptions**: domain errors ke liye `class InsufficientFunds extends Exception` (checked, jab caller ko recover karna chahiye) ya `extends RuntimeException` (unchecked, bug ya precondition violation). Constructor mein `super(message)` pass karo taaki `getMessage()` kaam kare; root cause ke liye `super(message, cause)` se chain karo.

**finally aur return**: try mein `return x;` ki value `finally` chalne se **pehle** evaluate karke rakh li jaati hai, isliye finally mein local variable badalne se returned value nahi badalti. Lekin agar `finally` khud `return` kare to woh try ki return value (aur koi bhi pending exception) ko overwrite kar deta hai; ye bad practice hai.

mistakes: `catch (Exception e)` sabse upar likhna. Neeche ke specific catches unreachable ho jaate hain (compile error) aur har error ek jaise handle hota hai.
Exception pakad kar chupchaap nigal jaana (`catch (Exception e) {}`). Bug chhup jaata hai; kam se kam log karo, ya cause ke saath ek meaningful exception dobara phenko.
`finally` mein `return` likhna. Ye try ki return value aur exception dono ko gayab kar deta hai; finally ko sirf cleanup ke liye rakho.
revision: `RuntimeException` aur uske subclasses unchecked; baaki `Exception` checked.
Checked: handle karo ya `throws` se declare karo.
Pehla matching catch hi chalta hai; specific catch pehle likho.
`finally` lagbhag hamesha chalta hai.
try ki return value finally se pehle tay hoti hai; finally ka `return` sab overwrite karta hai.
`throw` = phenkna, `throws` = declare karna.

weeks.title: Threads, Race Conditions and synchronized
weeks.summary: Is week aap Java mein threads banana (Thread vs Runnable), `start()` vs `run()`, `join()`, race conditions kyun hoti hain, `synchronized` se mutual exclusion, aur `volatile` se visibility ki guarantee seekhoge.
concepts: **Thread banana**: `Runnable` implement karo (ya lambda do) aur use `new Thread(r)` mein pass karo, ya `Thread` extend karke `run()` override karo. `Runnable` wala tareeka behtar hai: class kisi aur class ko extend kar sakti hai, aur task (kya karna hai) thread (kaise chalana hai) se alag rehta hai.

**`start()` vs `run()`**: `start()` naya thread banata hai jo `run()` ko apne alag call stack par chalata hai. Seedha `t.run()` sirf ek normal method call hai jo calling thread (jaise `main`) mein hi chalta hai. Ek hi thread object par `start()` doosri baar call karna `IllegalThreadStateException` deta hai.

**Scheduling aur `join()`**: threads ka interleaving OS aur JVM decide karte hain; jab tak aap synchronize na karo, output order ki koi guarantee nahi. `t.join()` current thread ko tab tak rokta hai jab tak `t` khatam na ho, aur `t` ke saare writes join ke baad dikhne ki guarantee bhi deta hai.

**Race condition**: `count++` ek atomic step nahi hai: read, add, write. Do threads same value padh kar dono +1 likhein to ek update kho jaata hai (lost update). Result run-to-run badalta hai, isliye aise bugs testing mein aksar chhup jaate hain.

**`synchronized`**: har object ke paas ek intrinsic lock (monitor) hota hai. `synchronized` instance method `this` ka lock leta hai, `static synchronized` method class object (`Counter.class`) ka, aur `synchronized (obj) { ... }` block `obj` ka. Ek lock ek waqt mein ek hi thread ke paas hota hai, isliye critical section mutually exclusive ban jaata hai. Ye lock reentrant hai: jis thread ke paas lock hai woh use dobara le sakta hai.

**Visibility aur `volatile`**: bina synchronization ke, ek thread ka write doosre thread ko kabhi na dikhe, ye bhi allowed hai (CPU caches, compiler/JIT reordering). `volatile` field ka har write uske baad hone wale reads ko dikhne ki guarantee deta hai, isliye stop-flag jaise cases ke liye sahi hai. Par `volatile` `count++` ko atomic **nahi** banata.

**Same lock zaroori**: mutual exclusion tabhi milta hai jab saare threads **ek hi** object ka lock lein. Alag objects par synchronized methods ek doosre ko nahi rokte; shared static data ke liye class-level lock ya ek common lock object chahiye.

`sold()` bhi synchronized hai taaki padhte waqt latest value dikhe (yahan `join` bhi ye visibility guarantee deta hai).
Answer: synchronized version mein hamesha **10000**; unsafe version mein koi guarantee nahi (≤ 10000).

mistakes: Thread chalane ke liye `t.run()` call karna. Koi naya thread nahi banta, code `main` mein sequentially chalta hai. `t.start()` likho.
`volatile int count` ko thread-safe counter samajhna. `count++` phir bhi teen alag steps hai; `synchronized` ya `AtomicInteger` chahiye.
Har thread ke liye alag object par `synchronized` method call karna jabki data static/shared hai. Locks alag hain to koi protection nahi; ek common lock ya `static synchronized` use karo.
revision: `start()` = naya thread; `run()` = normal method call.
`join()` = thread khatam hone tak wait.
`count++` atomic nahi: read-modify-write.
`synchronized` = ek lock, ek thread; sabko same object ka lock lena chahiye.
`volatile` = visibility, atomicity nahi.

weeks.title: Coordination: wait/notify, Deadlock and Concurrent Collections
weeks.summary: Is week aap threads ke beech coordination (`wait`, `notify`, `notifyAll`), producer–consumer pattern, deadlock ki chaar conditions aur unhe todna, aur thread-safe collections (`ConcurrentHashMap`, `BlockingQueue`) seekhoge.
concepts: **Coordination kyun**: kabhi ek thread ko doosre ka intezaar karna hota hai (consumer ko item aane ka, producer ko jagah khaali hone ka). Busy-waiting (`while (empty) {}`) bekaar mein CPU jalata hai; Java ka monitor iske liye `wait()`/`notify()` deta hai.

**`wait()`**: sirf us object ka lock pakde hue (uske `synchronized` block/method ke andar) call ho sakta hai, warna `IllegalMonitorStateException`. `wait()` lock **chhod deta hai** aur thread ko us object ke wait set mein sula deta hai; jagne ke baad lock dobara milne par hi thread aage badhta hai.

**`notify()` vs `notifyAll()`**: `notify()` wait set se koi ek thread jagata hai (kaunsa, iski guarantee nahi), `notifyAll()` sabko. Jab alag-alag conditions ke liye threads same object par wait karte hon (producers aur consumers dono), `notifyAll()` safe choice hai; `notify()` galat type ka thread jaga kar 'lost wakeup' de sakta hai.

**Hamesha `while` loop mein wait**: `while (queue.isEmpty()) lock.wait();`. Spurious wakeup ho sakta hai, aur jaagne tak koi aur thread condition phir se badal sakta hai. `if` se check karoge to jaag kar galat state mein aage badh jaoge.

**Producer–consumer**: ek bounded buffer jahan producer full hone par wait karta hai, consumer empty hone par, aur har change ke baad `notifyAll()`. Production code mein ise khud likhne ke bajaye `BlockingQueue` (`ArrayBlockingQueue`, `LinkedBlockingQueue`) use karo: `put()` full queue par block karta hai, `take()` empty par; `offer()` aur `poll()` block nahi karte, turant `false`/`null` dete hain.

**Deadlock**: chaar conditions ek saath hon tab hota hai: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait. Sabse practical fix circular wait todna hai: saare threads locks ek hi global order mein lein (jaise hamesha chhoti account id wala lock pehle). `ReentrantLock.tryLock` with timeout bhi ek option hai.

**Thread-safe collections**: `ArrayList`/`HashMap` thread-safe nahi hain. `Collections.synchronizedList` har method ko lock karta hai, par iterate karte waqt bahar se `synchronized (list)` chahiye. `ConcurrentHashMap` concurrent access aur atomic compound operations (`merge`, `compute`, `putIfAbsent`) deta hai; par `get` ke baad `put` do alag calls hain, unka combination atomic nahi. Read-heavy lists ke liye `CopyOnWriteArrayList`.

`if (empty) wait();` likhna. Spurious wakeup ya doosre consumer ki wajah se thread jaag kar empty queue se remove karne lagega. Hamesha `while` loop lagao.
Do threads ka locks ulte order mein lena (T1: A phir B, T2: B phir A). Ye circular wait se deadlock ka classic recipe hai; ek global lock order tay karo.

Deadlock: mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait.
`put`/`take` block karte hain; `offer`/`poll` turant return karte hain.
`ConcurrentHashMap.merge` atomic hai; `get` + `put` atomic nahi.

weeks.title: Executors, Futures, Atomics and Immutability
weeks.summary: Is week aap raw threads ki jagah thread pools (`ExecutorService`), `Callable` aur `Future` se results lena, atomic variables, immutable objects se thread safety, aur poore course ka ek design-level recap seekhoge.
concepts: **Raw threads ki problem**: har task ke liye `new Thread` banana mehenga hai, threads ki ginti control nahi hoti, aur result ya exception wapas lene ka koi seedha tareeka nahi. **Executor framework** task (kya karna hai) ko execution policy (kitne threads, kis order mein) se alag karta hai.

**Thread pools**: `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(n)` n reusable worker threads aur ek task queue deta hai; `newSingleThreadExecutor()` ek thread jo tasks submission order mein chalata hai. `execute(Runnable)` fire-and-forget hai, `submit(...)` ek `Future` deta hai. Kaam khatam hone par `shutdown()` (naye tasks band, queue wale poore) aur `awaitTermination(...)`; `shutdown` ke baad submit karne par `RejectedExecutionException`.

**`Callable` vs `Runnable`**: `Runnable.run()` kuch return nahi karta aur checked exception nahi phenk sakta. `Callable<V>.call()` `V` return karta hai aur `throws Exception` declare karta hai. Task ke andar aayi exception `Future.get()` par `ExecutionException` mein wrap hokar milti hai.

**`Future`**: pending result ka handle. `get()` result aane tak block karta hai, `get(timeout, unit)` time limit ke saath; `isDone()` aur `cancel(...)` bhi hain. `invokeAll(tasks)` sab tasks chala kar unke futures **usi order** mein deta hai jis order mein tasks diye the, completion order mein nahi. Non-blocking chaining ke liye `CompletableFuture` hai.

**Atomic variables**: `AtomicInteger`, `AtomicLong`, `AtomicReference` lock ke bina compare-and-set (CAS) instruction se `incrementAndGet()`, `addAndGet()`, `compareAndSet(expected, update)` jaise operations atomic banate hain. Ek variable ke counter ke liye ye `synchronized` se halka hai; par kai variables ko saath mein consistent rakhna ho to lock phir bhi chahiye.

**Immutability**: jo object banne ke baad kabhi badalta hi nahi, use bina lock ke threads share kar sakte hain. Recipe: class `final`, saare fields `private final`, koi setter nahi, mutable inputs ki **defensive copy** (`List.copyOf`), aur getters se mutable internals bahar na do. `String`, `Integer`, `LocalDate` immutable hain, aur Java 16+ ka `record` shallowly immutable hai.

**Course recap**: encapsulation (private state + methods), inheritance aur interfaces se abstraction, dynamic dispatch se polymorphism, generics se type safety, collections aur comparators se data handling, exceptions se error contracts, aur concurrency mein shared mutable state ko kam karna: immutable data, thread-safe collections, aur executors.

Har task ke liye submit ke turant baad `get()` call karna (submit → get → submit → get). Isse parallelism khatam ho jaata hai; pehle saare tasks submit karo, phir results lo.
Sochna ki `final` fields wali class apne aap immutable hai. Agar field ek mutable `List` hai aur bahar wala reference share hai, to content badal sakta hai; defensive copy lo.

Immutable = final class, private final fields, defensive copies.
